poēta, poētae m.

noun, first declension

The ordinary word in prose and verse. In Plautus also a contriver, a schemer (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • poētria, poētriae f. — poetess, woman poet

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Cael. 64: fābulārum poētria (Lewis & Short); Traupman 168

  • vātēs, vātis m./f. — poet, bard; prophet

    declension · also used · classical · Verg. E. 7.27 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Hor.)

    First a seer or prophet; the old name for a poet, fallen out of use until Vergil restored it to honour (Lewis & Short). The poet as inspired singer, not the everyday word.

Examples

  • meminī super Pindarō poētā et Vergiliō in hunc fermē modum disserere

    I remember him talking about Pindar the poet and Vergil roughly like thisGell. 17.10.1

  • etiam dicta clārōrum virōrum et ēlēctōs ex poētīs maximē … locōs ēdiscere inter lūsum licet

    even sayings of famous men and passages chosen mostly from the poets can be learned by heart while playingQuint. 1.1.36

See also poetry, song, recite.
